{
  "configuration": {
    "values": [],
    "output": {
      "summary": "Application $(.execution.input.resourceName) is STARTED with instances:$(\"\\n\")$(if .execution.input.rollingRestart  then .rollingRestart.output.resourceInstancesStates else .simpleRestart.output.resourceInstances end | map(\"\\t• Instance \\(.resourceInstance) is \\(.state)\") | join(\"\\n\"))",
      "previousResourceInstancesState": "$(.getAppState.output.resourceInstances)",
      "previousDesiredState": "$(.getAppState.output.desiredState)",
      "previousResourceInstancesStates": "$(.getAppState.output.resourceInstances)",
      "resourceInstancesStates": "$(if .rollingRestart.executed then .rollingRestart.output.resourceInstancesStates else .simpleRestart.output.resourceInstancesStates end)"
    },
    "executors": [
      {
        "execute": "cf-sapcp:ResolveCfIds:1",
        "input": {
          "resourceGroup": "$(.execution.input.resourceGroup)",
          "password": "$(.execution.input.password)",
          "resourceName": "$(.execution.input.resourceName)",
          "region": "$(.execution.input.region)",
          "user": "$(.execution.input.user)",
          "subAccount": "$(.execution.input.subAccount)",
          "identityProvider": "$(.execution.input.identityProvider)",
          "refreshToken": "$(.execution.input.refreshToken)"
        },
        "alias": "resolveCfIds",
        "progressMessage": null,
        "initialDelay": null,
        "pause": null,
        "when": null,
        "validate": null,
        "autoRetry": null,
        "repeat": null,
        "errorMessages": []
      },
      {
        "execute": "applm-sapcp:GetCfAppState:2",
        "input": {
          "resourceGroup": "$(.resolveCfIds.output.spaceId)",
          "password": "$(.execution.input.password)",

certificateAuthorityData.description: Base64 encoded Certificate Authority data, e.g trusted certificates used for SSL (TLS) authentication against Kubenetes API server

headers.description: Comma separated key-value pairs like JSON object representing request headers (values are not secret), e.g. Content-Type: application/json , Accept:, etc.

method.description: Http method used for the request. E.g GET, POST, etc

namespace.description: A Kubernetes namespace within a specified cluster

password.description: Password used for Basic Auth

path.description: Represents path parameters as part of the URL, e.g /param, /param1, /example/resource, etc. Path chain must always start with a slash '/' symbol and after that this symbol must be used as separator between other values.

query.description: Represents query parameters as part of the URL, e.g ?query=value1, query=value2, etc.

resourceName.description: Describes the name of defined Kubernetes resource. E.g pod-name, service-name

resourceType.description: The type of the defined Kubernetes resource. Has to be a noun in plural form, e.g pods, services, deployments, etc.

server.description: URL for the Kubernetes API server

successResponseCodes.description: An array describing the response codes which will be used to treat this HTTP request as successful, e.g. ["2xx", "3xx", "404"]. Default value is ["2xx"]

token.description: Bearer token used during the HTTP authentication process. Note: this overwrites all other authentication mechanisms

user.description: User used for Basic Auth

authorizationHeader.description: Explicit value for the HTTP Authorization header. This overwrites all other authentication mechanisms.

body.description: The payload of the HTTP request

clientCert.description: A client certificate which contains a private key and one or more X.509 certificates. The value needs to be in PEM format, and it may optionally be Base64-encoded.

csrfUrl.description: An optional CSRF URL which will be used to obtain an X-CSRF-TOKEN via a GET request

headers.description: The request headers. The values are not sensitive. Examples: Content-Type, Accept, Authorization. If the Authorization header is provided, it will overwrite the 'user' and 'password' values.

ignoreResponseBody.description: When set to true, the response body is omitted from the command output. Use this to avoid execution size limit failures when the response body is not needed. This setting is independent of 'omitBodyInErrorMessage'.

method.description: The HTTP method to be used for the request. Examples: GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH

omitBodyInErrorMessage.description: Whether the response body should be excluded from the error message when the HTTP request fails. Set this to true if you want to avoid sensitive data exposure.

refreshToken.description: An already obtained OAuth 2.0 refresh token which will be used to get a new access token via the Refresh Token grant type. Related input keys: 'clientId', 'clientSecret', 'tokenUrl'

responseBodyTransformer.description: A dynamic expression used to transform the response body string. If you need to use it as an object, it must be parsed, for example, using 'toObject'. The result replaces the original response body. Do not put the expression in the $() construct.

routeOauthThroughScc.description: When set to true, routes OAuth token requests through the SAP Cloud Connector. This setting does not affect routing of the main HTTP request.

sccEnabled.description: When set to true, enables the routing of HTTP requests through the SAP Cloud Connector to reach private endpoints

sccLocationId.description: Specifies the Cloud Connector instance over which the connection should be opened in scenarios where multiple connectors are available. If not specified, the connection is opened to the Cloud Connector that is connected without any location ID.

sccTechnicalUserPropagation.description: Enables the use of technical user propagation when making calls through the SAP Cloud Connector. You can set it to true only if 'sccEnabled' is also true, and if an OAuth authentication flow is used.

succeedOnTimeout.description: Prevents the command from failing in case of a timeout. If set to true, the response of the timed-out request will have body 'null', the response headers will be '{}', and the response status code will be '-1'.

successResponseCodes.description: The response codes which will be used to treat this HTTP request as successful. Example: ["2xx", "3xx", "404"]

timeout.description: An optional execution timeout in seconds

tokenType.description: Specifies the type of OAuth 2.0 token to use for authentication. 'ACCESS' uses an access token for authorizing the HTTP request, while 'ID' uses an ID token. Defaults to 'ACCESS'.

tokenUrl.description: An OAuth 2.0 server token URL endpoint which supports the chosen OAuth flow. If the 'tokenUrl' key is not provided, Basic authentication will be used (see 'user' and 'password').

trustAnyCert.description: When set to true, allows all TLS server certificates to be trusted for this HTTP request, including CSRF and token endpoints. Do not enable this in productive environments.

trustedCerts.description: One or more trusted server X.509 certificates. The value needs to be in PEM format, and it may optionally be Base64-encoded.

url.description: The target HTTP URL to be used for the request

user.description: The name of a technical user or an OAuth 2.0 client ID used for authentication. Related input keys: 'password' or 'tokenUrl'

I inspected its contract and the relevant executor behavior. The required caller inputs follow that contract; credentials stay protected and no operation has been executed. Inspected required caller keys: plan:string, service:string, serviceKey:object, subAccountId:string. Outputs: entitlement:object. Optional credentials and scope keys remain as declared. SetEntitlement:2 sets an absolute amount or enables/disables a boolean entitlement; enable and amount are mutually exclusive. IncreaseQuotaEntitlement:2 adds an increment and is unsuitable for an absolute target. The inspected wrapper delegates its write to hidden SendEntitlementRequest:1 and checks its asynchronous job with bounded checkStatus repetition; a PUT receipt alone is not completion.

body.description: The payload of the HTTP request

clientCert.description: A client certificate which contains a private key and one or more X.509 certificates. The value needs to be in PEM format, and it may optionally be Base64-encoded.

headers.description: The request headers. The values are not sensitive. Examples: Content-Type, Accept, Authorization. If the Authorization header is provided, it will overwrite the 'user' and 'password' values.

method.description: The HTTP method to be used for the request. Examples: GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH

omitBodyInErrorMessage.description: Whether the response body should be excluded from the error message when the HTTP request fails. Set this to true if you want to avoid sensitive data exposure.

password.description: The password for the specified technical user or the client secret for the specified OAuth 2.0 client ID used for authentication. Related input keys: 'user' or 'tokenUrl'

refreshToken.description: An already obtained OAuth 2.0 refresh token which will be used to get a new access token via the Refresh Token grant type. Related input keys: 'clientId', 'clientSecret', 'tokenUrl'

responseBodyTransformer.description: A dynamic expression used to transform the response body string. If you need to use it as an object, it must be parsed, for example, using 'toObject'. The result replaces the original response body. Do not put the expression in the $() construct.

timeout.description: An optional execution timeout in seconds

tokenUrl.description: An OAuth 2.0 server token URL endpoint which supports the chosen OAuth flow. If the 'tokenUrl' key is not provided, Basic authentication will be used (see 'user' and 'password').

trustAnyCert.description: When set to true, allows all TLS server certificates to be trusted for this HTTP request, including CSRF and token endpoints. Do not enable this in productive environments.

trustedCerts.description: One or more trusted server X.509 certificates. The value needs to be in PEM format, and it may optionally be Base64-encoded.

commands/http-sapcp:HttpRequest:1.description: Execute an HTTP request. Supported authentication methods: Custom Authorization Header; OAuth 2.0 Client Credentials, Password, and Refresh Token Grant Flows; Basic Authentication; IAS Technical User Certificate Authentication; no authentication.

authorizationHeader.description: Explicit value for the HTTP Authorization header. This overwrites all other authentication mechanisms.

body.description: The payload of the HTTP request

clientCert.description: A client certificate which contains a private key and one or more X.509 certificates. The value needs to be in PEM format, and it may optionally be Base64-encoded.

clientId.description: An OAuth 2.0 client ID used for authentication. Related input keys: 'clientSecret', 'tokenUrl'

clientSecret.description: The client secret for the specified OAuth 2.0 client ID used for authentication. Related input keys: 'clientId', 'tokenUrl'

csrfUrl.description: An optional CSRF URL which will be used to obtain an X-CSRF-TOKEN via a GET request

headers.description: The request headers. The values are not sensitive. Examples: Content-Type, Accept, Authorization. If the Authorization header is provided, it will overwrite the 'user' and 'password' values.

ignoreResponseBody.description: When set to true, the response body is omitted from the command output. Use this to avoid execution size limit failures when the response body is not needed. This setting is independent of 'omitBodyInErrorMessage'.

method.description: The HTTP method to be used for the request. Examples: GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH

omitBodyInErrorMessage.description: Whether the response body should be excluded from the error message when the HTTP request fails. Set this to true if you want to avoid sensitive data exposure.

password.description: The password for the specified technical user or the client secret for the specified OAuth 2.0 client ID used for authentication. Related input keys: 'user' or 'tokenUrl'

refreshToken.description: An already obtained OAuth 2.0 refresh token which will be used to get a new access token via the Refresh Token grant type. Related input keys: 'clientId', 'clientSecret', 'tokenUrl'

responseBodyTransformer.description: A dynamic expression used to transform the response body string. If you need to use it as an object, it must be parsed, for example, using 'toObject'. The result replaces the original response body. Do not put the expression in the $() construct.

routeOauthThroughScc.description: When set to true, routes OAuth token requests through the SAP Cloud Connector. This setting does not affect routing of the main HTTP request.

sccEnabled.description: When set to true, enables the routing of HTTP requests through the SAP Cloud Connector to reach private endpoints

sccLocationId.description: Specifies the Cloud Connector instance over which the connection should be opened in scenarios where multiple connectors are available. If not specified, the connection is opened to the Cloud Connector that is connected without any location ID.

sccTechnicalUserPropagation.description: Enables the use of technical user propagation when making calls through the SAP Cloud Connector. You can set it to true only if 'sccEnabled' is also true, and if an OAuth authentication flow is used.

succeedOnTimeout.description: Prevents the command from failing in case of a timeout. If set to true, the response of the timed-out request will have body 'null', the response headers will be '{}', and the response status code will be '-1'.

successResponseCodes.description: The response codes which will be used to treat this HTTP request as successful. Example: ["2xx", "3xx", "404"]

timeout.description: An optional execution timeout in seconds

tokenType.description: Specifies the type of OAuth 2.0 token to use for authentication. 'ACCESS' uses an access token for authorizing the HTTP request, while 'ID' uses an ID token. Defaults to 'ACCESS'.

tokenUrl.description: An OAuth 2.0 server token URL endpoint which supports the chosen OAuth flow. If the 'tokenUrl' key is not provided, Basic authentication will be used (see 'user' and 'password').

trustAnyCert.description: When set to true, allows all TLS server certificates to be trusted for this HTTP request, including CSRF and token endpoints. Do not enable this in productive environments.

trustedCerts.description: One or more trusted server X.509 certificates. The value needs to be in PEM format, and it may optionally be Base64-encoded.

url.description: The target HTTP URL to be used for the request

user.description: The name of a technical user or an OAuth 2.0 client ID used for authentication. Related input keys: 'password' or 'tokenUrl'

reference.answer: Choose the managed admin API binding, distinguishing managed metrics APIs and SQL DBADMIN credentials; report sensitive output. Recommended ID hanacloud-sapcp:ObtainHanaCloudManagedAdminApiBinding:1. I inspected its contract and the relevant executor behavior. The required caller inputs follow that contract; credentials stay protected and no operation has been executed. Inspected required caller keys: environmentType:string. Outputs: bindingId:string, serviceKey:object sensitive. Optional credentials and scope keys remain as declared. This recommendation inspects definitions only; no provisioning or backing execution was performed. Dependency guarantees beyond the inspected definition are unverified. ObtainHanaCloudManagedAdminApiBinding:1 manages admin-api-access, while ObtainHanaCloudManagedApiBinding is for metrics/alerts/metering and ObtainHanaCloudSqlBinding is DBADMIN SQL access. The newest admin binding is reused until the inspected one-month rotation threshold, old bindings beyond two months are pruned, and x509 validity is three months. Cloud Foundry uses region/org/space with user/password, while Other Environment needs the appropriate serviceKey; the wrapper may provision supporting entitlement/service/binding resources when actually executed.

reference.answer: Choose the scope-based upgrade and explain its successful no-op contract; do not confuse it with an upgrade that fails on no target. Recommended ID hanacloud-sapcp:UpgradeHanaCloudInstanceByScope:1. I inspected its contract and the relevant executor behavior. The required caller inputs follow that contract; credentials stay protected and no operation has been executed. Inspected required caller keys: environmentType:string, instanceId:string, updateStrategy:string, upgradeScope:string. Outputs: currentVersion:string, instanceId:string, snapshotId:string, targetVersion:string, upgraded:string. Optional credentials and scope keys remain as declared. This recommendation inspects definitions only; no provisioning or backing execution was performed. Dependency guarantees beyond the inspected definition are unverified. UpgradeHanaCloudInstanceByScope:1 selects latestPatch, latestTrack or nextTrack; when pickVersion is empty its upgradeInstance executor is skipped and upgraded=false is a successful no-op. UpgradeHanaCloudInstance:1 is excluded because its validation rejects an absent applicable version. Snapshot rotation is conditional on both an eligible target and explicit rotateSnapshot permission. A FINISHED parent alone does not prove upgraded=true.

reference.answer: Choose point-in-time recovery and exclude snapshot revert or restart; surface resource scope and destructive recovery behavior. Recommended ID hanacloud-sapcp:RecoverHanaCloudInstanceToPointInTime:1. I inspected its contract and the relevant executor behavior. The required caller inputs follow that contract; credentials stay protected and no operation has been executed. Inspected required caller keys: environmentType:string, instanceId:string, targetTimestamp:string. Outputs: instanceId:string. Optional credentials and scope keys remain as declared. This recommendation inspects definitions only; no provisioning or backing execution was performed. Dependency guarantees beyond the inspected definition are unverified. The point-in-time recovery target must be inside configured backup retention, not in the future and not earlier than the oldest retained data backup. Snapshot recovery is a distinct operation and cannot substitute a timestamp without evidence. An accepted recovery is not proof of final recovered state; execution/read-back requires separate authorization.

successResponseCodes.description: An array describing the response codes which will be used to treat the request as successful, e.g. ["2xx", "3xx", "404"]

timeout.description: An optional execution timeout in seconds applied per individual HTTP request

sccLocationId.description: Specifies the Cloud Connector instance over which the connection should be opened in scenarios where multiple connectors are available. If not specified, the connection is opened to the Cloud Connector that is connected without any location ID.

sccTechnicalUserPropagation.description: Enables the use of technical user propagation when making calls through the SAP Cloud Connector. You can set it to true only if 'sccEnabled' is also true, and if an OAuth authentication flow is used.

succeedOnTimeout.description: Prevents the command from failing in case of a timeout. If set to true, the response of the timed-out request will have body 'null', the response headers will be '{}', and the response status code will be '-1'.

successResponseCodes.description: The response codes which will be used to treat this HTTP request as successful. Example: ["2xx", "3xx", "404"]

timeout.description: An optional execution timeout in seconds

tokenType.description: Specifies the type of OAuth 2.0 token to use for authentication. 'ACCESS' uses an access token for authorizing the HTTP request, while 'ID' uses an ID token. Defaults to 'ACCESS'.

tokenUrl.description: An OAuth 2.0 server token URL endpoint which supports the chosen OAuth flow. If the 'tokenUrl' key is not provided, Basic authentication will be used (see 'user' and 'password').

trustAnyCert.description: When set to true, allows all TLS server certificates to be trusted for this HTTP request, including CSRF and token endpoints. Do not enable this in productive environments.

trustedCerts.description: One or more trusted server X.509 certificates. The value needs to be in PEM format, and it may optionally be Base64-encoded.

url.description: The target HTTP URL to be used for the request

user.description: The name of a technical user or an OAuth 2.0 client ID used for authentication. Related input keys: 'password' or 'tokenUrl'

reference.answer: Choose the sensitive HTTP response variant; sensitive request credentials alone do not protect ordinary response output. Recommended ID http-sapcp:SensitiveHttpRequest:1. I inspected its contract and the relevant executor behavior. The required caller inputs follow that contract; credentials stay protected and no operation has been executed. Inspected required caller keys: method:string, url:string. Outputs: body:string sensitive, headers:object sensitive, method:string, size:number, status:number, time:number, url:string sensitive. Optional credentials and scope keys remain as declared. This recommendation inspects definitions only; no provisioning or backing execution was performed. Dependency guarantees beyond the inspected definition are unverified.

The required caller inputs follow that contract; credentials stay protected and no operation has been executed. Inspected required caller keys: apiHost:string, clientId:string, clientSecret:string, iflowId:string, targetEnvironment:string, tokenUrl:string. Outputs: finalStatus:string, iflowId:string, parameterUpdateResults:array sensitive, partnerUpsertResults:array, targetEnvironment:string. Optional credentials and scope keys remain as declared. This recommendation inspects definitions only; no provisioning or backing execution was performed. Dependency guarantees beyond the inspected definition are unverified.

commands/http-sapcp:HttpRequest:1.description: Execute an HTTP request. Supported authentication methods: Custom Authorization Header; OAuth 2.0 Client Credentials, Password, and Refresh Token Grant Flows; Basic Authentication; IAS Technical User Certificate Authentication; no authentication.

authorizationHeader.description: Explicit value for the HTTP Authorization header. This overwrites all other authentication mechanisms.

body.description: The payload of the HTTP request

clientCert.description: A client certificate which contains a private key and one or more X.509 certificates. The value needs to be in PEM format, and it may optionally be Base64-encoded.

clientId.description: An OAuth 2.0 client ID used for authentication. Related input keys: 'clientSecret', 'tokenUrl'

clientSecret.description: The client secret for the specified OAuth 2.0 client ID used for authentication. Related input keys: 'clientId', 'tokenUrl'

csrfUrl.description: An optional CSRF URL which will be used to obtain an X-CSRF-TOKEN via a GET request

headers.description: The request headers. The values are not sensitive. Examples: Content-Type, Accept, Authorization. If the Authorization header is provided, it will overwrite the 'user' and 'password' values.

ignoreResponseBody.description: When set to true, the response body is omitted from the command output. Use this to avoid execution size limit failures when the response body is not needed. This setting is independent of 'omitBodyInErrorMessage'.

method.description: The HTTP method to be used for the request. Examples: GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH

omitBodyInErrorMessage.description: Whether the response body should be excluded from the error message when the HTTP request fails. Set this to true if you want to avoid sensitive data exposure.

password.description: The password for the specified technical user or the client secret for the specified OAuth 2.0 client ID used for authentication. Related input keys: 'user' or 'tokenUrl'

refreshToken.description: An already obtained OAuth 2.0 refresh token which will be used to get a new access token via the Refresh Token grant type. Related input keys: 'clientId', 'clientSecret', 'tokenUrl'

responseBodyTransformer.description: A dynamic expression used to transform the response body string. If you need to use it as an object, it must be parsed, for example, using 'toObject'. The result replaces the original response body. Do not put the expression in the $() construct.

routeOauthThroughScc.description: When set to true, routes OAuth token requests through the SAP Cloud Connector. This setting does not affect routing of the main HTTP request.

sccEnabled.description: When set to true, enables the routing of HTTP requests through the SAP Cloud Connector to reach private endpoints

sccLocationId.description: Specifies the Cloud Connector instance over which the connection should be opened in scenarios where multiple connectors are available. If not specified, the connection is opened to the Cloud Connector that is connected without any location ID.

sccTechnicalUserPropagation.description: Enables the use of technical user propagation when making calls through the SAP Cloud Connector. You can set it to true only if 'sccEnabled' is also true, and if an OAuth authentication flow is used.

succeedOnTimeout.description: Prevents the command from failing in case of a timeout. If set to true, the response of the timed-out request will have body 'null', the response headers will be '{}', and the response status code will be '-1'.

successResponseCodes.description: The response codes which will be used to treat this HTTP request as successful. Example: ["2xx", "3xx", "404"]

timeout.description: An optional execution timeout in seconds

tokenType.description: Specifies the type of OAuth 2.0 token to use for authentication. 'ACCESS' uses an access token for authorizing the HTTP request, while 'ID' uses an ID token. Defaults to 'ACCESS'.

tokenUrl.description: An OAuth 2.0 server token URL endpoint which supports the chosen OAuth flow. If the 'tokenUrl' key is not provided, Basic authentication will be used (see 'user' and 'password').

trustAnyCert.description: When set to true, allows all TLS server certificates to be trusted for this HTTP request, including CSRF and token endpoints. Do not enable this in productive environments.

trustedCerts.description: One or more trusted server X.509 certificates. The value needs to be in PEM format, and it may optionally be Base64-encoded.

url.description: The target HTTP URL to be used for the request

user.description: The name of a technical user or an OAuth 2.0 client ID used for authentication. Related input keys: 'password' or 'tokenUrl'

reference.answer: Choose WaitJenkinsBuild for the existing build identity; Execute/Trigger would start additional work. Recommended ID jenkins-sapcp:WaitJenkinsBuild:1. I inspected its contract and the relevant executor behavior. The required caller inputs follow that contract; credentials stay protected and no operation has been executed. Inspected required caller keys: build:number, jenkinsUrl:string, job:string, password:string, user:string. Outputs: buildData:object, status:string. Optional credentials and scope keys remain as declared. This recommendation inspects definitions only; no provisioning or backing execution was performed. Dependency guarantees beyond the inspected definition are unverified. WaitUntilBuildJobIsFinished:1 waits for the caller-selected existing build and does not trigger another build. TriggerBuildJob:1 is excluded because it starts work. Inspect the terminal result separately: UNSTABLE differs from SUCCESS and a stopped building flag alone is not a business-success guarantee. Waiting is bounded and a missing/unauthorized build must fail rather than retrigger it.

reference.answer: Choose the Deployment restart with polling and distinguish trigger-only and wrong-resource alternatives. Recommended ID kubernetes-sapcp:RestartKubernetesDeployment:1. I inspected its contract and the relevant executor behavior. The required caller inputs follow that contract; credentials stay protected and no operation has been executed. Inspected required caller keys: name:string, namespace:string. Outputs: status:object. Optional credentials and scope keys remain as declared. This recommendation inspects definitions only; no provisioning or backing execution was performed. Dependency guarantees beyond the inspected definition are unverified. PollRestartKubernetesResource:1 waits for the rollout readiness conjunction: deployments/statefulsets need desired, updated and ready replica counts to agree; daemonsets use their distinct scheduled/ready counters. A restart/patch receipt alone is not readiness. The wait is bounded, and a missing counter or an authorization error must not become successful readiness. KubernetesApiRequest:1 alone does not provide this terminal-state wait.

region.description: Cloud Foundry region of the instance, e.g. cf-eu10. Required only when 'environmentType' is 'Cloud Foundry'.

artifact.description: Reusable Upgrade an SAP HANA Cloud instance to a target version determined by the chosen upgrade scope on its current release cycle. Optionally rotates a snapshot beforehand for a fresh restore point. If no version matches the chosen scope, no changes are made.

deadline.description: Maximum time in minutes to wait for the upgrade to complete.

environmentType.description: Where an SAP HANA Cloud instance lives. Use 'Cloud Foundry' for instances created in a Cloud Foundry space, or 'Other Environment' for instances created via SAP Service Manager at the subaccount level.

identityProvider.description: Identity provider used to authenticate the Cloud Foundry user. Defaults to SAP ID Service (sap.ids). For a custom IdP, use the origin key shown in your subaccount.

instanceId.description: Name or GUID of an SAP HANA Cloud instance to upgrade.

org.description: Cloud Foundry organization where the instance lives. Accepts a name or GUID. Required only when 'environmentType' is 'Cloud Foundry'.

password.description: Password for the Cloud Foundry user. Required only when 'environmentType' is 'Cloud Foundry'.

region.description: Cloud Foundry region of the instance, e.g. cf-eu10. Required only when 'environmentType' is 'Cloud Foundry'.

rotateSnapshot.description: When set to true, rotates a snapshot before the upgrade by deleting the oldest snapshot and creating a new one, to provide a fresh restore point. If no version matches the chosen scope, no snapshot is rotated.

serviceKey.description: A service key used to authenticate to SAP HANA Cloud instances in other environments. Provide a service key for either SAP Service Manager or SAP Cloud Management service (cis). When using a cis service key, also provide 'subAccountId'.

space.description: Cloud Foundry space where the instance lives. Accepts a name or GUID. Required only when 'environmentType' is 'Cloud Foundry'.

subAccountId.description: GUID of the BTP subaccount that holds an SAP HANA Cloud instance. Provide it when authenticating with an SAP Cloud Management service (cis) service key.

updateStrategy.description: Whether the change is applied with an instance restart ('with_restart') or without ('without_restart').

upgradeScope.description: Which upgrade to look for on the instance's current release cycle. 'latestPatch' picks the highest patch on the current track. 'latestTrack' picks the highest patch on the highest available track. 'nextTrack' picks the highest patch on the lowest track different from the current one. If nothing matches the chosen scope, the command completes without making changes.

user.description: Cloud Foundry user for authentication. Required only when 'environmentType' is 'Cloud Foundry'.
